items.title: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages
items.desc: Clayton’s warning comes ahead of Thanksgiving travel, after separate outages disrupted air travel, Microsoft 365 and some bank transactions.

items.title: Is Annie Andrews Too Real for the Senate? South Carolinians Are About to Find Out.
items.desc: The pediatrician, who once compared JD Vance to the herpes virus, notched one of the most shocking upsets of the midterm elections by defeating Senator Darline Graham.

items.title: FAA Says All Delta Flights Delayed as Automated System Falters
items.desc: The system facing problems is used to calculate the weight and balance of departing flights. The disruptions come after a nationwide ground stop that canceled thousands of flights last weekend.

items.title: International climate talks end in disappointment
items.desc: Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement after conflict over fossil fuels - the primary driver of fossil fuels.

items.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Nov. 22): The Food Issue
items.desc: Jane Pauley hosts our annual "Eat, Drink & Be Merry" holiday broadcast exploring all things epicurean! Check out our menu...

items.title: How a Crash Into a Cruise Ship in New Orleans Became a ‘Miracle on the Mississippi’
items.desc: When a 525-foot tanker struck the docked American Heritage riverboat on Nov. 13, a rescue operation turned tragedy into triumph and led the nearly 200 aboard to safety.

items.title: Jeffries talks about where Democrats may be able to work with Trump
items.desc: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries outlined areas where Democrats "can explore coming together" with President Trump.

items.title: St. Patrick’s Day Parade Canceled as Florida Figures Out D.E.I. Law
items.desc: Cities and counties are pulling funding from groups and events they’ve long supported before a new law bars them from promoting diversity, equity and inclusion activities.

items.title: Nature: Turkeys in New Hampshire
items.desc: We leave you this Sunday with turkeys on the run in Rye, New Hampshire. Videographer: Michael Clark.

items.title: Guri guri: A Hawaiian favorite
items.desc: The ingredients that go into the Hawaiian dessert guri guri – creamier than sherbet and lighter than ice cream – are a closely-guarded family secret. But on the island of Maui, where it's been served for generations, it's also a way of life. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.

items.title: Just add water: Creating food for the great outdoors
items.desc: Freeze-dried and dehydrated foods have become popular with hikers for their outdoor adventures. Correspondent Conor Knighton witnesses the processes used to turn entire meals – from beef stroganoff to chicken cashew curry – into backpackable bags.

items.title: I’ve studied over 200 kids—parents who do 6 things accidentally raise people pleasers: It starts in ‘ordinary, well-intentioned moments’
items.desc: Reem Raouda, a conscious parenting coach who's worked with over 200 families, shares six habits worth reconsidering, like treating disagreement as disrespect.

items.title: Sallie Ann Robinson on preserving Gullah cuisine
items.desc: On a barrier island off the coast of South Carolina, Sallie Ann Robinson – chef, cookbook writer, and human whirlwind – sees food as one way to preserve Gullah Geechee culture. Correspondent Martha Teichner talks with Robinson, winner of this year's James Beard Foundation Hall of Fame Book Award.

items.title: How cottage cheese was made sexy
items.desc: For decades, cottage cheese was a bland, low-calorie diet food. But now social media influencers are spicing it up, adding cottage cheese to everything from pancakes to pizza crust, and demand has exploded. Correspondent David Pogue looks at how the protein craze has made a familiar dairy product … sexy.

items.title: Kwame Onwuachi's culinary journey
items.desc: Award-winning chef Kwame Onwuachi's Tatiana, located in New York's Lincoln Center, was named the best restaurant in the city by The New York Times two years in a row. Onwuachi discusses his Afro-Caribbean menu, and his path to becoming one of today's brightest culinary stars, with correspondent Nancy Giles.

items.title: Home-cooked meals, to go
items.desc: In California, more than 1,300 small kitchens are licensed to make and sell food. These MEHKOs (short for "micro enterprise home kitchen operations") are run out of homes, allowing cooks to pursue their passions, make supplementary income, or test out potential dining concepts without the investment required for food trucks or traditional brick-and-mortar restaurants. Correspondent Luke Burbank talked with some of the home chefs who turn family recipes into culinary passion projects.

items.title: Social Security benefits are rising in 2027, but other changes could affect what you keep
items.desc: A 3.6% Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for 2027 will increase benefits across the board. But Medicare and tax changes will also affect retirees.

items.title: How Brussels sprouts lost their bitterness
items.desc: In the old days, Brussels sprouts were not exactly a favorite vegetable. But today they're a runaway hit, thanks to science.

items.title: Wisconsin's supper clubs, where community is always on the menu
items.desc: Chain restaurants put a lot of America's supper clubs out of business in the 1950s and '60s, but the family-run dinner establishments continue to thrive in Wisconsin, built on Midwestern hospitality and friendliness. Correspondent Mo Rocca reports.

items.title: Taking on credit card debt to buy food
items.desc: According to a recent survey, about 35% of Americans are using credit cards to buy increasingly expensive groceries – and many are having trouble paying off that food debt.

items.title: Taking on credit card debt to buy food
items.desc: This Thanksgiving, Americans are paying 32% more for food compared to what we paid in 2020. But according to a recent survey, about 35% of us are using credit cards to buy groceries – and many are having trouble paying off that food debt. Correspondent Lee Cowan looks at how rising costs, and the ease of Buy Now Pay Later apps, contribute to ever-tighter food budgets.

items.title: A Riverboat Captain Recalls a Crash on the Mississippi
items.desc: Capt. Len Stewart had mere seconds to react before a 525-foot tanker crashed into the American Heritage, a riverboat in New Orleans with nearly 200 passengers on board.

items.title: 26-year-old Google worker earns $323,000 a year—but lives on less than minimum wage
items.desc: Charles Broomfield set a post-college goal of reaching $750,000 in investments by age 30. Now 26, he expects to get there within the next year.
